topic: Closed-form sharp harm bounds for stayers under ordered multilayer selection. Fix any finite L>=2, randomized Z, D_z in {0,...,L} with D_1>=D_0, binary Y observed when D>0, unrestricted potential-outcome dependence, and an observable positive lower bound on total positive-layer stayer mass. Characterize the exact joint region of layer-stayer masses s_d and harm masses h_d; prove the stayer diagonal is the Cartesian box ell_d=max(0,C_d-R_{d-1})<=s_d<=u_d=min(r_d,c_d), derive jointly attainable hinge bounds (s_d-a_d)_+<=h_d<=min(s_d,b_d), and obtain O(L) closed-form sharp endpoints for the fraction harmed among D_0=D_1>0 plus the iff certificate q_0d-q_1d>R_d-C_d for unavoidable harm. Give exact confidence-region projection and directional numerical-delta inference at ties and structural zero cells. Consumer: KMV's Job Corps/WorkAdvance multilayer Lee analyses and Lee-bounds software. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Derived the Cartesian diagonal projection by strict-triangular residual transport, the simultaneous binary-outcome completion, and closed-form endpoint ratios. Exact L=2 bounds are [8/25,10/11]; an all-positive L=3 example gives [1/9,10/11]. A 31-arc missing-outcome network has a valid decoder, and 180 independent programs for L=2 through 7, including zero cells, matched the formulas below 1.5e-15. Checked KMV, Possebom--Riva, Kallus, Khandamiryan--Semenova, and generic transport precedents; none supplied the all-layer joint box and contraction. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove conditional bounded-Lipschitz validity of the joint endpoint numerical-delta bootstrap at every fixed observable law, including simultaneous hinge equalities and structural zero cells, using the ambient formula extension and a defined fallback outside the positive-denominator neighborhood. EARLY KILL TEST: Independently enumerate small rational L=3 margins with zero masses and compare both closed-form endpoints against the full 31-arc expanded-state ratio program; any mismatch in the Cartesian projection or simultaneous outcome completion stops the paper. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_multilayer_stayer_harm.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp joint identified region for positive-layer stayer masses and binary-outcome harm masses under ordered multilayer selection, and determine whether its aggregate fraction-harmed projection has closed-form endpoints.

source_refs.claim: The paper introduces multilayer sample selection and obtains sharp within-layer mean-effect bounds from dependent mixture equations, but does not study cross-world harm masses.
source_refs.author: Kory Kroft, Ismael Mourifié, and Atom Vayalinkal

source_refs.claim: The paper derives sharp probability-of-causation bounds among always-observed units under randomized treatment and monotone sample selection, but selection is binary rather than multilayered.
source_refs.author: Vitor Possebom and Flavio Riva

source_refs.claim: The paper derives sharp bounds on the fraction negatively affected by treatment from observed outcome marginals, without endogenous multilayer selection.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kroft–Mourifié–Vayalinkal preserve cross-layer restrictions but target linear within-layer mean effects; Possebom–Riva and Kallus preserve the binary cross-world outcome coupling needed for harm but collapse observation to one always-observed stratum or omit selection. Searches for multilayer selection together with fraction harmed, probability of causation, and stayer-specific harm returned these strands separately and no combined characterization. The missing proof object is the simultaneous projection of the ordered triangular transition polytope and every binary potential-outcome completion: coordinatewise feasible stayer and harm masses need not be jointly feasible a priori, and the aggregate target has an unidentified denominator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observable-law formula for the exact joint polytope of layer-stayer and harm masses, accompanied by a constructive sharpness argument and closed-form lower and upper endpoints for the aggregate fraction harmed among positive-layer stayers.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation begins with Job Corps wage selection, explains why a binary observation indicator hides economically important sorting across layers, and turns that failure into a sharp partial-identification problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Randomized job training changes whether wages are observed -> workers also sort across heterogeneous employment layers -> binary Lee bounds mix causal and sorting effects -> layer-specific latent response types and their harm masses must be bounded jointly.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the two-step mixture-equation construction that first characterizes response-type probabilities jointly across layers and then completes conditional outcome distributions while preserving cross-equation dependence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed region has the same ordered multilayer response-type skeleton, with binary cross-world outcome cells added to every diagonal type.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the combination of Lee/Horowitz–Manski mixture bounds and Fréchet completion of binary potential outcomes for the always-observed stratum.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the binary-selection version of a cross-world probability target; the new work must replace its single always-observed mass with a jointly constrained vector of layer-stayer masses.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt robust influence-function estimation of sharp harm-bound functionals, including cross-fitting and conservative validity under nuisance misspecification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the multilayer endpoints are identified, they remain sharp bounds on a causal fraction harmed and require inference that respects endpoint nonsmoothness.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish pointwise conditional bounded-Lipschitz validity of a joint numerical-directional-delta bootstrap for multilayer stayer-harm endpoints at simultaneous hinge ties and structural-zero observable cells.

source_refs.claim: For directionally but not fully differentiable maps, the ordinary bootstrap generally fails and valid resampling requires estimating the directional derivative.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: The numerical delta method consistently estimates laws of directionally differentiable transforms and is uniformly valid for certain convex Lipschitz maps.
source_refs.author: Han Hong and Jessie Li

source_refs.claim: Tiered benefit and harm bounds exhibit nonregularity when individualized optimizers are tied, including null-effect or immune subpopulations, motivating stabilized inference.
source_refs.author: Johan de Aguas, Sebastian Krumscheid, Johan Pensar, and Guido Biele
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 275

open_problems.why_unsolved: The endpoint vector is a ratio of finite maxima, minima, and positive-part hinges, so simultaneous equalities create multiple active branches while zero cells place the multinomial limit on a lower-dimensional face. Fang–Santos supplies the general directional-differentiability diagnostic, and Hong–Li supplies numerical differentiation, but Hong–Li's stated uniform result covers certain convex Lipschitz maps rather than a coupled lower/upper ratio map with a denominator-neighborhood fallback. De Aguas et al. address optimizer ambiguity for tiered harm using stabilized one-step corrections, not structural zeros induced by ordered selection margins. Searches combining numerical delta methods, structural zeros, multilayer Lee bounds, and fraction harmed found no theorem covering this fixed-law boundary case.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving the endpoint vector's explicit Hadamard directional derivative on the multinomial tangent cone and proving conditional bounded-Lipschitz convergence of the joint numerical-delta bootstrap, including an ambient formula extension and a defined fallback outside the positive-denominator neighborhood.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames harm probabilities as decision-relevant but partially identified and makes optimizer ambiguity and exceptional laws the central inferential problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Individual benefit and harm depend on unobserved joint potential outcomes -> sharp bounds remain decision-relevant -> ties in bound optimization create nonregularity -> stable inference must remain valid at exceptional laws and structural boundaries.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the directional functional delta method and bootstrap an estimated directional derivative rather than the original nondifferentiable map, proving validity through conditional weak convergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The stayer-harm endpoints are finite-dimensional directionally differentiable transforms of observable multinomial probabilities.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate the directional derivative by evaluating the endpoint formula at a shrinking numerical perturbation along each bootstrap draw, with step-size conditions separating sampling noise from approximation error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired software can evaluate the closed-form endpoint map directly, avoiding bespoke code for every active-set derivative.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate bootstrap relaxations of moment constraints and project directly onto the scalar target, with uniform coverage over the maintained model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the benchmark confidence-region projection route against which a closed-form numerical-delta interval can be validated.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop a sharp sensitivity region for the multilayer stayer fraction harmed when ordered selection may fail by bounded layer-specific downward-transition masses.

source_refs.claim: The paper embeds departures from treatment exogeneity and monotone binary sample selection in interpretable sensitivity parameters and computes sharp ATE bounds by linear programming.
source_refs.author: Lukáš Lafférs and Roman Nedela

source_refs.claim: Generalized Lee bounds allow the sign of selection monotonicity to vary with pretreatment covariates and give inference for a support function, but retain binary selection and target mean effects.
source_refs.author: Vira Semenova

source_refs.claim: The paper parameterizes violations of LATE monotonicity by defier mass and outcome-distribution differences, derives sharp bounds, and defines robust regions with bootstrap confidence sets.
source_refs.author: Claudia Noack

open_problems.why_unsolved: Lafférs–Nedela permits violations of one binary selection-monotonicity restriction, Semenova permits a covariate-dependent sign for one binary selection margin, and Noack develops monotonicity-breakdown regions for one-dimensional IV compliance. Ordered multilayer selection instead has many distinct forbidden cells with D1<D0, and the harm target depends jointly on the diagonal masses and binary outcome couplings. A scalar violation budget does not determine its distribution across layer distances, while separate layerwise budgets interact through common row and column margins. Searches surfaced no sensitivity analysis preserving sharpness for a cross-world harm ratio under multilayer selection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified-set and breakdown-frontier characterization indexed by a vector or weighted sum of downward-transition masses, with computable endpoints for the stayer fraction harmed and an observable certificate for which violation budgets overturn unavoidable harm.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates sensitivity analysis as the operational response to a contestable Lee monotonicity assumption and uses interpretable violation parameters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Lee bounds are sharp and simple -> their exogeneity and monotonicity assumptions may be disputed -> encode departures using interpretable budgets -> report how the sharp substantive conclusion changes across the sensitivity region.

method_exemplars.technique: Augment the latent response-type linear program with constraints measuring departures from exogeneity and monotonicity, then optimize the target over compatible joint laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Downward multilayer transitions are directly representable as previously forbidden latent cells subject to budget constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a robust region over monotonicity-violation parameters and bootstrap its boundary instead of reporting sensitivity bounds at one arbitrary parameter value.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired deliverable is naturally a breakdown frontier for the conclusion that some harm is unavoidable.

method_exemplars.technique: Test feasibility of nonnegative solutions to large known-coefficient linear systems through a geometric inequality characterization, using linear programs and uniform size control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sensitivity model enlarges a finite latent-cell system whose feasibility changes with the downward-transition budgets.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend multilayer stayer-harm identification from binary outcomes to ordered categorical outcomes while retaining a sharp simultaneous characterization across all selection layers.

source_refs.claim: For K-tier outcomes, strong treatment monotonicity does not point-identify tiered benefit, and the paper gives sharp bounds and stabilized inference without sample-selection layers.
source_refs.author: Johan de Aguas, Sebastian Krumscheid, Johan Pensar, and Guido Biele
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 275

source_refs.claim: The paper gives sharp bounds for probabilities of beneficial and strictly beneficial treatment effects with ordinal outcomes under fixed potential-outcome marginals.
source_refs.author: Jiannan Lu, Peng Ding, and Tirthankar Dasgupta
source_refs.venue: Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics

source_refs.claim: The multilayer-selection framework derives within-layer treatment-effect bounds, but targets outcome means rather than ordinal cross-world harm probabilities.
source_refs.author: Kory Kroft, Ismael Mourifié, and Atom Vayalinkal

open_problems.why_unsolved: With binary outcomes, each layer's unknown joint potential-outcome law is a 2-by-2 table and its harm cell has a one-dimensional Fréchet interval. For K ordered categories, completion becomes a K-by-K transportation polytope, and simultaneous attainability across layers must coexist with uncertain diagonal selection masses. Lu–Ding–Dasgupta and de Aguas et al. solve ordinal coupling when the target population is observed without multilayer selection; Kroft–Mourifié–Vayalinkal solve multilayer mixture restrictions for mean effects. Searches combining ordinal or tiered harm with multilayer sample selection returned no paper joining the two.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp flow or polyhedral characterization of all layer-specific ordinal harm masses and computable endpoints for the probability of any worsening, or worsening by at least k tiers, among positive-layer stayers.

writing_exemplar.why: It explains why ordered categories make individual benefit and harm scientifically meaningful while leaving their cross-world probabilities unidentified.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average effects obscure crossings of meaningful outcome tiers -> tiered benefit and harm require joint potential outcomes -> observed marginals only partially identify those probabilities -> ordered observation layers add a second latent allocation problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use transportation-table duality and constructive couplings to obtain sharp probabilities of weak and strict benefit from ordinal marginal distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Within each fixed stayer layer, the destination target is an ordinal potential-outcome coupling problem whose marginal masses are themselves only partially allocated.

method_exemplars.technique: First solve the cross-equation response-type mixture problem and then impose outcome restrictions conditional on every response type.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the outer multilayer allocation argument into which the ordinal transportation completion must be inserted.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the stratum-specific stabilized one-step correction for nonregular tiered-bound functionals when multiple individualized optimizers tie.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The multilayer ordinal endpoint inherits tier-specific optimizer ambiguity, compounded by selection-layer allocation.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive covariate-assisted sharp bounds and orthogonal inference for the overall fraction harmed among multilayer stayers when ordered selection restrictions hold conditionally and some conditional layers have zero mass.

source_refs.claim: Conditional monotonicity and covariate-assisted generalized Lee bounds can sharply tighten mean-effect bounds, with low- and high-dimensional inference.
source_refs.author: Vira Semenova

source_refs.claim: Boundaries of covariate-indexed conditional linear programs can be represented as averages of intersections of regression functions and estimated as regular parameters.
source_refs.author: Gevorg Khandamiryan and Vira Semenova

source_refs.claim: Covariate stratification tightens fraction-harmed bounds, and robust influence-function inference accommodates flexibly learned nuisance functions when outcomes are not selectively observed.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus

source_refs.claim: Continuous and multivalued Lee bounds use orthogonal moments and cross-fitting under covariate-dependent sufficient treatment values, but target always-observed mean effects rather than harm.
source_refs.author: Ying-Ying Lee and Chu-An Liu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Semenova and Lee–Liu show how covariates alter selection monotonicity and tighten Lee-type mean bounds; Kallus handles covariate-assisted harm without endogenous observation; Khandamiryan–Semenova regularize averages of conditional linear-program values. The stayer fraction harmed is instead a ratio of integrated harm and stayer masses, not an average of conditional fractions, and the extremizing conditional stayer allocations may need coordination before aggregation. Conditional structural zeros also make naive layerwise ratios undefined. The first proof step that changes is the interchange of conditional optimization, integration, and linear-fractional projection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp formula showing how conditional joint support sets aggregate into population numerator and denominator bounds, together with a cross-fitted orthogonal estimator and a valid limit or confidence result allowing zero-mass conditional layers.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates covariate assistance both as a credibility repair for global monotonicity and as a source of tighter, empirically usable Lee bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unconditional Lee monotonicity can fail in heterogeneous populations -> its direction may remain credible within covariate strata -> conditional bounds exploit that structure -> multilayer harm requires aggregating conditional latent stayer populations rather than conditional means.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the response-type mixture construction conditionally on covariates to characterize cross-layer feasibility before optimizing outcome targets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resulting conditional support sets have the same multilayer skeleton, but must be aggregated before projecting the ratio target.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent an aggregated conditional-program boundary through intersections of regression functions and construct adaptive asymptotic theory for its estimated support function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The numerator and denominator support calculations are conditional finite linear programs whose population aggregation is the principal new inferential challenge.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct orthogonal influence-function scores for sharp harm bounds using sample splitting, with conservative validity under nuisance misspecification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies harm-specific orthogonalization machinery once the selectively observed conditional endpoint has been characterized.

literature_map:
1. Lee (2009, Review of Economic Studies, DOI 10.1111/j.1467-937X.2009.00536.x) is the foundational sharp trimming result for binary sample selection and Job Corps wages.
2. Kroft, Mourifié, and Vayalinkal (2024, NBER 32952/arXiv:2409.04589; revised 2026) replace binary selection with ordered layers and sharply bound within-layer mean effects using dependent mixture equations.
3. Their central warning is that canonical Lee bounds can mix within-layer causal effects with treatment-induced sorting across heterogeneous layers.
4. Possebom and Riva (2025, JBES, DOI 10.1080/07350015.2024.2388639) sharply bound probability of causation among always-observed units, but only for binary selection.
5. Kallus (2022, NeurIPS, arXiv:2205.10327) sharply bounds the fraction harmed and develops robust efficient inference, but does not allow endogenous multilayer observation.
6. Gadbury, Iyer, and Albert (2004, JSPI, DOI 10.1016/S0378-3758(03)00115-0) is an older anchor for nonidentified benefit and harm proportions with binary outcomes.
7. Frandsen and Lefgren (2021, Quantitative Economics, DOI 10.3982/QE1273) bound the treatment-effect distribution and fraction harmed under dependence restrictions, without sample selection.
8. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018, JEBS, arXiv:1507.01542) and de Aguas et al. (2025, CLeaR, arXiv:2502.10049) give sharp ordinal or tiered benefit-harm bounds; neither includes multilayer selection.
9. Semenova (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2008.12720) permits covariate-dependent selection-monotonicity direction and gives support-function inference for generalized Lee mean bounds.
10. Lee and Liu (2024, arXiv:2411.04312) extend Lee bounds to continuous or multivalued treatment with sufficient treatment values and DML inference, again targeting mean effects.
11. Lafférs and Nedela (2017, Economics Letters, DOI 10.1016/j.econlet.2017.06.039) relax binary Lee assumptions through sharp LP sensitivity analysis; Noack (2021, arXiv:2106.06421) supplies a monotonicity-breakdown-region template.
12. Fang and Santos (2019, Review of Economic Studies, arXiv:1404.3763) establish why ordinary bootstrap fails for nondifferentiable endpoint maps; Hong and Li (2018, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2018.06.007) provide the numerical directional delta method.
13. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica, arXiv:1601.00934) give calibrated projection inference, while Fang, Santos, Shaikh, and Torgovitsky (2023, Econometrica, arXiv:2009.08568) test feasibility of large nonnegative linear systems.
14. Khandamiryan and Semenova (2026, arXiv:2606.08359) make aggregated values of conditional linear programs regular, but the multilayer fraction-harmed target remains a nonsmooth linear-fractional projection.
15. Targeted searches consistently separated the relevant strands: multilayer-selection papers, harm or probability-of-causation papers, and boundary-valid inference papers each cover one or two components, but no located paper combines all three.
